Q: Add custom attribute to OpenAPI specification file and swagger in .net core web api A:

If you use Swashbuckle.AspNetCore, you can use a document filter to customise the OpenAPI document.

Q: SQL partiton by suppress repeating values A:

What database is this? On SQL Server, something like this would do:

select
  salesmanno, custname, amt
, case when subtotal_no = subtotal_count then subtotal end as subtotal
, case when total_no = total_count then subtotal end as total
from (
  select 
    h.salesmanno 
  , c.custname 
  , h.amt 
  , sum(h.amt) over (partition by salesmanno) as subtotal
  , sum(h.amt) over (partition by null) as grandtotal
  , row_number() over (partition by salesmanno order by custname) as subtotal_no
  , row_number() over (partition by null order by salesmanno, custname) as as total_no
  , count(*) over (parition by salesmanno) as subtotal_count
  , count(*) over (parition by null) as total_count
  from hdr h, cust c 
  WHERE h.custno = c.custno 
    and h.hdate = '6/8/2009'
  ) a
order by total_no

Shorter version, more sorting for the database, maybe less obvious what's going on:

select
  salesmanno, custname, amt
, case when subtotal_no = 1 then subtotal end as subtotal
, case when total_no = 1 then subtotal end as total
from (
  select 
    h.salesmanno 
  , c.custname 
  , h.amt 
  , sum(h.amt) over (partition by salesmanno) as subtotal
  , sum(h.amt) over (partition by null) as grandtotal
  , row_number() over (partition by salesmanno order by custname desc) as subtotal_no
  , row_number() over (partition by null order by salesmanno desc, custname desc) as as total_no
  from hdr h, cust c 
  WHERE h.custno = c.custno 
    and h.hdate = '6/8/2009'
  ) a
order by total_no desc

Alternatively, using ROLLUP to generate subtotal and total rows:

  select 
    h.salesmanno 
  , c.custname 
  , sum(h.amt) as amt
  from hdr h, cust c 
  WHERE h.custno = c.custno 
    and h.hdate = '6/8/2009'
  group by 
    h.salesmanno 
  , c.custname 
  with rollup 
  order by
    h.salesmanno 
  , c.custname

To get the results in the proper order, change the order by to something like this:

  order by
    grouping(h.salesmanno)
  , h.salesmanno
  , grouping(c.custname)
  , c.custname

Q: CLion with WSL toolchain: std::string and standard headers unresolved in editor A:

When you say it compiles, do you mean internally with the IDE's configuration?

The code inspection feature in Jetbrains IDEs can simply choose to use something else than the build feature and it's been a solid source of frustration for me too. I don't think compile_commands.json will matter. Rather, you should look in IDE/project settings' XMLs, it could have wrong paths at higher priority than toolchain paths.

Q: Is it safe to use the stack below esp? A:

Is it safe to move the value to [esp - 2]

Using an offset like that will definitely expose the data to corruption any time any action on the thread needs to touch the stack again. This can occur during interrupts, APCs, context switches, exceptions, etc.
What you'll want to do instead is to actually reserve space on the stack and save a pointer to it:

sub  esp, 4       ; Always move it in 4-byte increments. (x64 may need 8 bytes)
mov  eax, esp     ; EAX points to your 4-byte buffer
...               ; << Here you use the memory
add  esp, 4       ; Restore allocation.

Of course if you only need a few bytes, the push and pop instructions offer a more compact solution:

push eax          ; Create allocation
mov  eax, esp     ; EAX points to a 4-byte buffer properly aligned to system
...               ; << Here you use the memory
pop  eax          ; Restore allocation

Q: Should I use a .JSON file to store data in a C++ game A:

On the whether to use JSON or not, that is an "it depends" question. If your data needs to be accessible to other processes or shared across hosts, networks, etc.., then JSON is convenient and is generally supported by some library available to each language. The downside to it is, it will require some additional library to read/write in C/C++. It is also not a space/byte efficient storage format.

If you have data you need to read/write in your game, determine how you are holding that data in memory and write it out in a manner it can be read back in without filtering though a JSON or other library. If on the other hand, you have sharing needs or simply want to standardize around JSON for your data files, there is nothing wrong with that either, you will just lose an incremental amount of processing used to convert to/from json. Binary files also require additional BSON handling.

So, it's up to you, but I've always tried to fit the storage format to how I use the data and do it in the most efficient way possible. That said, I'm happy to use JSON when dealing with mongdb, and other systems that use JSON. Match your data handling to your data and the constraints imposed by the environment your game will operate in.
